doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Do some jazz players not fit together?

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: What about the feel? Is there a… can classical people feel jazz and vice versa?
Jesus, I have no idea. You have to ask… I’m sure it’s different. I imagine. But…
Are there jazz people who just don’t fit together because their internal feel or style is just incompatible with another player?
I don’t, I don’t know. What, what would be your take on that, seriously?
I… seriously, I think there must be people that just don’t have the same sense of…

…of time. I don’t mean keeping time but that, the feel. Their sense of, I don’t know, to use expressions that I probably shouldn’t. But, you know, one’s sense of where the groove is is not someone else’s or…
Yeah. I’m sure… just like… that’s how people are, right? (laughs)
Some people you get along with; other people you say, “Schmuck! I don’t like you.” (laughs)
Was there anybody that you, for instance, might enjoy listening to but wouldn’t want to play with?
